newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record in morning.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index roared to a record high on Tuesday, as shares in HSBC Holdings Plc surged following the banking giant's better-than-expected interim results.
The blue chip index hit an all-time high of 16,482.74, before paring its gains later to trade up 135.78 points, or 0.84 percent, at 16,395.37.
Turnover was HK$8.04 billion after the first hour of trade.

HSBC shares were up HK$7.00 at HK$271.00 after rising to an early high of HK$273.00. It lost HK$4.00 on Monday before announcing a 13 percent rise in pretax profit for the first six months of the year to 2.62 billion sterling.
"The bank's results were above expectations so the stock has moved up more than it lost yesterday," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
Au-Young said it was difficult to say where the Hang Seng Index was heading after it burst into record ground on Tuesday.
"We are in a major bull run. 16,500 is not the limit but may be initial resistance," said Au-young.

But Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said he was surprised that the strength of the rally had fizzled so rapidly. "Most of the market's gains are in HSBC and the rest of the market is lagging," he said.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$88.00 and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$77.75.
Jardine Matheson Ltd and Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that Cheung Kong and Hutchison had bought shares in both companies.
"Although for the time being we do not know their intention, this represents a good opportunity for them," said Au-Young of Cheung Kong and Hutchison.
"They should know if this is a profitable investment."
Hang Seng Bank Ltd fell HK$0.50 to HK$110.50 after posting a 14.5 percent rise in interim net profit to HK$4.98 billion.
